questions.q: What are "Liquidated Damages"?
o: The total value of a project after it has been liquidated.
A pre-agreed amount paid by the contractor for every day of delay.
The amount spent by the contractor for unforeseen site damages.
The professional fee deducted when the architect fails to perform.
questions.n: Liquidated damages are a specific sum stipulated in the contract to be paid as compensation for each day the project exceeds the completion date.

questions.q: What is the Architect's fee for "Repetitive Construction" for the 2nd unit?
questions.n: In the scale of repetitive work provided, the second identical unit is charged at half of the basic fee.

questions.q: What is the fee for the 3rd unit in repetitive construction?
questions.n: In this specific descending scale, the fee drops from 50% for the second unit to 40% for the third.

questions.q: What is the fee for the 4th and succeeding units in repetitive construction?
questions.n: The scale plateaus at 30% for all units after the third in this repetitive work scenario.

questions.q: Which SPP Document covers Post-Construction Services?
questions.n: Document 205 outlines the scope for services rendered after the building is completed, such as maintenance.

questions.q: What is the fee for Post-Construction Services (Full-time supervision)?
questions.n: Full-time supervision fees under post-construction services are typically calculated as a percentage within the 1% to 1.5% range of the construction cost.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the "Structural Conceptualization" of a building?
questions.n: Under RA 9266, structural conceptualization is explicitly defined as part of the architect's scope of practice.

questions.q: What is the PCC?
questions.n: PCC stands for Project Construction Cost, which serves as the basis for percentage-based architectural fees.

questions.q: Which permit is required before starting any construction activity?
questions.n: The Building Permit is the primary legal authorization required from the OBO to begin work.

questions.q: What is an "Ancillary Permit"?
o: Permits for specific disciplines (Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing) attached to the building permit.
A permit for fences and sidewalks.
A permit for temporary construction sheds.
The final permit required to use the building.
questions.n: Ancillary permits cover specialized technical fields required for the building's operation.

questions.q: What is an "Accessory Permit"?
o: Permit required for interior design work.
Permit for electrical and plumbing lines.
For structures like fences, sidewalks, or towers.
A permit for additional parking space only.
questions.n: Accessory permits are for separate structures that are not part of the main building but are on the same site.

questions.q: What document is a requirement for the Occupancy Permit that records daily activities?
questions.n: The construction logbook is a legally required daily record signed by the architect in charge of construction.

questions.q: When is an Occupancy Permit issued?
o: After the architect is paid in full.
Upon completion of the building and inspection by the OBO.
Immediately after the Building Permit is granted.
questions.n: The Office of the Building Official must inspect the finished structure to ensure it matches the approved plans.

questions.q: What is the fee for a "Monumental Project" under DAEDS?
questions.n: Group 5 projects, which are monumental or highly intricate, carry the highest standard fee of 12%.

questions.q: What is the fee for "Residential" (Group 1) under DAEDS?
questions.n: Under current SPP guidelines for single-detached residences, the professional fee is 10%.

questions.q: Who is the "Owner" in a construction contract?
o: The person or entity that orders the work.
questions.n: The owner is the client who initiates the project and is responsible for financing it.

questions.q: Who is the "Prime Professional" in a building project?
questions.n: As the coordinator of all engineering and design disciplines for a building, the architect is the prime professional.

questions.q: What is the MOC?
questions.n: MOC refers to how the architect's professional services are paid for (e.g., Lump Sum, Percentage).

questions.q: What is the fee for "Airport" projects under DADS?
questions.n: Under the specific fee structure provided for these complex structures, the rate is 7%.

questions.q: What is the percentage of the fee for the "Schematic Design Phase"?
questions.n: Schematic Design accounts for 15% of the total architectural fee under standard progress billing.

questions.q: Under BP 344, what is the minimum dimension of an accessible toilet?
questions.n: BP 344 specifies these dimensions to ensure sufficient room for a wheelchair and assistance.

questions.q: What is the minimum dimension of an elevator car according to BP 344?
questions.n: This size allows for a wheelchair to enter and have enough depth for the user and an attendant.

questions.q: In BP 344, what is the maximum height of a signage for the visually impaired?
questions.n: Signage must be within this specific range for tactile reading to be accessible.

questions.q: Under PD 1096 (NBCP), what is the maximum length of a dead-end corridor?
questions.n: To prevent entrapment during an emergency, the NBCP limits dead-end corridors to 6 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum area for a habitable room?
o: 6.00 sqm with a minimum dimension of 2.00m.
questions.n: The National Building Code requires at least 6 square meters for rooms intended for living.

questions.q: What is the minimum area for a kitchen?
o: 3.00 sqm with a minimum dimension of 1.50m.
questions.n: Kitchens are given a smaller minimum area than habitable rooms under the NBCP.

questions.q: What is the minimum area for a T&B?
o: 1.20 sqm with a minimum dimension of 0.90m.
questions.n: The NBCP requires a minimum of 1.2 square meters for a toilet and bath area.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a Single Detached (Open Market)?
questions.n: Open Market single-detached lots under PD 957 must be at least 120 square meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum lot area for a Single Detached (Socialized Housing/BP 220)?
questions.n: Socialized housing units have smaller lot requirements to keep the housing affordable.

questions.q: What is the lot frontage for a regular corner lot in PD 957?
questions.n: Corner lots require more frontage to accommodate the two street exposures and setbacks.

questions.q: In planning, who is the proponent of the "Garden City Movement"?
questions.n: Howard's book 'Garden Cities of To-morrow' proposed self-contained communities surrounded by greenbelts.

questions.q: Who is known for the "City Beautiful Movement" and the planning of Manila/Baguio?
questions.n: Burnham is famous for the motto 'Make no little plans' and designed the initial layouts for Manila and Baguio.

questions.q: Who proposed the "London Plan" and the concept of "Greenbelts"?
questions.n: Abercrombie was responsible for the Greater London Plan of 1944 which introduced the greenbelt concept.

questions.q: What is a "Site Development Plan"?
o: A plan showing only the floor layout of the building.
A technical description of the lot boundaries.
A plan showing the building's facade and height.
A plan showing the layout of the building, roads, and utilities on the site.
questions.n: The SDP illustrates the relationship between the structure and its immediate environment and infrastructure.

questions.q: What is the ideal ratio of lot length to width for a subdivision?
questions.n: A 2:1 ratio is generally considered the most efficient and versatile for subdivision planning.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what monsoon brings rain from the Southwest (June to Oct)?
questions.n: The Habagat monsoon brings moist and warm air from the southwest, causing the rainy season.

questions.q: What monsoon brings cool air from the Northeast (Nov to Feb)?
questions.n: The Amihan monsoon brings cooler temperatures and less rain from the Northeast.

questions.q: What is a "Tropical Climate" characteristic regarding humidity?
questions.n: Tropical maritime climates, like the Philippines, are characterized by high levels of moisture in the air.

questions.q: What is the best orientation for a rectangular building in the Philippines to minimize heat gain?
o: Long axis running East to West (facades face North and South).
Long axis running North to South
Short axis running East to West
questions.n: By orienting the short ends to the East and West, you minimize direct solar exposure from the rising and setting sun.

questions.q: Under RA 9514 (Fire Code), what is a device used to detect smoke?
questions.n: Smoke detectors specifically sense the presence of smoke as an early warning for fire.

questions.q: What does FDAS stand for?
questions.n: FDAS is the complete system used to detect a fire and alert the occupants.

questions.q: In BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for a Rowhouse?
questions.n: BP 220 sets smaller minimums for rowhouses to maximize density and affordability.

questions.q: What is the "non-leasable" area percentage often cited in subdivision planning?
questions.n: Standard planning practices often allocate 30% of the gross area to non-leasable open space like roads and parks.

questions.q: What is "Urban Planning"?
o: The technical and political process concerned with the use of land and design of the urban environment.
Designing individual houses for a neighborhood.
A list of rules for construction safety.
The study of historical buildings in a city.
questions.n: Urban planning integrates policy, engineering, and design to manage city growth and resources.

questions.q: What is "City Planning"?
o: A sub-set of urban planning focusing specifically on the needs of a city.
Planning for the interior layout of a city hall.
Building a shopping mall in a city.
questions.n: City planning is more localized than urban planning, focusing on the specific systems and land use within city limits.

questions.q: In Tropical Architecture, what is "Cross Ventilation"?
o: The circulation of fresh air through a building from one side to the other.
Air trapped in a ceiling to provide insulation.
Ventilation through a single small window.
The use of air conditioning to cool a room.
questions.n: Cross ventilation requires inlets and outlets on opposite or adjacent walls to let wind pass through.

questions.q: What is the height of a handrail for a ramp under BP 344?
questions.n: BP 344 requires two handrail heights to accommodate users of different heights and those in wheelchairs.

questions.q: What is the maximum slope of a ramp for PWDs?
questions.n: The 1:12 ratio is the maximum allowed slope for an accessible ramp.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a corridor for PWDs?
questions.n: 1.20 meters is the minimum width allowed for an accessible corridor.

questions.q: Which document specifies the legal relationship between the Owner and the Architect?
questions.n: The signed Service Agreement is the legal binding document between the client and the professional.
